grand_strategy.reading:
Taiwan is Luttwak's textbook case of a state whose survival rests on two
things it does not control: being indispensable and a guarantor's ambiguity.
The first is real (the leading edge of chips and AI servers) but is traded
away piece by piece to secure the second, and the second is now openly priced:
the Trump administration holds a USD 14bn arms package as a negotiating chip,
says it does not want anyone to 'go independent', and sat down with Xi twice
in 2026 without a word on Taiwan in the White House fact sheet. Beijing, for
its part, has moved from the exercise to the rehearsal of a blockade (Joint
Sword 2024, Strait Thunder 2025A, Justice Mission 2025), and from the
president to the institutions: legal punishment of 'diehards', a channel to
the KMT, and cable and coast-guard pressure in the grey zone. The grade toward
China is therefore rival and not adversary only because Taipei's declared aim
is to be left as it is, not to end the Chinese state, while Beijing's aim is
the end of Taiwan's separateness: the pair is asymmetric on purpose. The home
front is the third hinge: a president whose party lost the legislature, saw
the recalls fail and the budget cut, and whose own parliament now steers part
of the defence plan. Signals that are not rows: no PLA mega-exercise has
followed the Washington summit, air activity is half of 2025 while ships
stay, and Honduras has not decided. The question for 2027 is whether chips
remain a shield or become only a price.

stances.note: Rival and not adversary, on purpose. Beijing claims the island, rehearses its blockade (Joint Sword 2024, Strait Thunder-2025A on 1-2 Apr 2025, Justice Mission-2025 on 29-31 Dec 2025, the closest live fire so far), punishes 'Taiwan independence diehards' (14 named plus 12 accomplices by 7 Jan 2026, rules of 21 Jun 2024 that allow the death penalty in absentia) and presses in the grey zone (cable cuts, coast guard). Taipei's own government calls China a 'foreign hostile force' (17 measures, 13 Mar 2025), which is the strongest source for the hostility, but its declared aim is to be left as it is and to talk 'on an equal and dignified footing' (Lai, 1 Jan 2026), not to end the Chinese state or its regime, so the mortal-enemy grade does not fit from Taipei's side; the ROC constitution's claim over the mainland is dormant, so claimed_territory does not apply either. The pair is asymmetric: Beijing's aim is the end of Taiwan's separateness. Trend stable: air activity in 2026 is half of 2025 while ships stay, Xi met KMT chair Cheng on 10 Apr 2026, and no named exercise has followed the Trump-Xi summits. No source uses the word 'rival' for Taipei's view: our reading (confidence C). Bond - kin: language, history and a shared civil war, which makes the pair a feud; Xi calls Taiwanese 'one family'.

stances.note: Ally by structure, reluctant by friction. relations_to.summary: The Taiwanese Representative Office in Vilnius keeps its 2021 name while Lithuania's government and president dispute whether it should become the 'Taipei' office; Taiwan said in Feb 2026 there were no talks on a rename, and a coalition partner argued in June 2026 for changing it within two months after notifying the US.

relations_to.summary: In Feb 2026 Philippine, US and Japanese aircraft drilled over the Bashi Channel; Taiwan did not take part. In Aug 2025 Marcos said the Philippines would be pulled into any war over Taiwan.
